Implementer notes (Claude Opus 5.5, the lead). Use them as context only; the judgment is yours.

Scope: spec `pose-assess-leaves-sealed-checkouts-alone` (R1–R4, decisions D1–D2, residual limit L1 in the Final Report). Reviewer runs used to fail with "the run changed files in the sealed worktree" after a planned `pose assess` persisted `.pose/assessments/*` and `.pose/state/*` into the sealed checkout.
- R1: `pose assess discover|integrate|tech-debt --no-persist` prints the result without writing (`internal/cli/assess.go`, `assessPersists`).
- R2: in the sealed checkout of a delegated review (`POSE_SEALED_CHECKOUT`, already set by the dispatch) those commands never persist and say so on standard error; `init`, `snapshot` and `request` refuse. The Store's assessment writers (`SaveComponentState`, `GenerateConsolidatedAssessment`, `SaveIntegrationMatrix`, `SaveTechDebtReport`) also refuse there (`internal/pose/assessment_sealed.go`).
- R3: the review plan's assessment tools carry `--no-persist` (`reviewToolArgs`).
- R4: `TestAssessLeavesTheSealedCheckoutUnchanged` hashes the whole tree before and after every command.
Each guard has a test that failed with it mutated out. The full `go test ./...` of `pose-mcp` passed.

Please check in particular that no assess path still writes in a sealed checkout, that `--update-state` cannot bypass the guard, and that persisting runs outside a sealed checkout behave as before.

The planned assessment tools of this bundle now carry `--no-persist`, so you may run them in the sealed checkout: that is also a live test of R2 and R3.

Before you finish, run `"$POSE_REVIEW_CLI" review draft-check --draft -` on your final message (pipe it on standard input) and fix every reason it reports.

Draft format rules, enforced by the conclusion preflight:
- New findings use short unprefixed IDs (N1, N2, …). Round-prefixed IDs go only in `prior_findings`, and only for the findings the brief lists under "Findings to account for", with exactly id, status and evidence.
- Structural-delta mappings go inside the criterion that answers them, with `basis` set to a requirement or a decision of this spec (R1–R4, D1, D2).
- A criterion scoped to a component cites evidence from that component only.

Sandbox limits: the checkout is sealed and read-only. Never `cd`; keep the checkout root as the working directory. Keep test runs focused (`go -C pose-mcp test ./internal/cli ./internal/pose -run 'Assess|ReviewPlanRunsAssessments'`, `go -C pose-mcp vet ./internal/cli ./internal/pose`), and let every command you start finish before you end: a process still running when you end makes the run unconcludable. A tool you cannot rerun in the sandbox is a limit of the run, not a defect of the subject: cite the sealed evidence that covers it, then decide on the code itself.
